new_statements.quote: 1.3. Touchant les tons — De nombreux changements tonals peuvent être observés dans nos exemples ; le seul changement systématique que nous ayons pu observer est le remplacement du ton modulé descendant par un ton haut. [ex. 87 'médicament' (emprunt au kanuri): vieux kə̀rgûŋ / jeunes kùrgúŋ] — La langue, appelée [màlgbè], du même nom que la localité, appartient au sous-groupe septentrional du groupe dit 'KOTOKO', de la branche centrale du tchadique.
new_statements.translation: 1.3. Concerning tones — Many tonal changes can be observed in our examples; the only systematic change we were able to observe is the replacement of the falling contour tone by a high tone. [ex. 87 'medicine' (Kanuri loan): old speakers kə̀rgûŋ / young speakers kùrgúŋ] — The language, called [màlgbè], with the same name as the locality, belongs to the northern subgroup of the so-called 'KOTOKO' group, of the Central branch of Chadic.

new_statements.locator: §1.3 'Touchant les tons' (HAL author-manuscript p. 7; journal pagination 123-135, exact page not recoverable from the manuscript); identity sentence in the opening paragraph (p. 2)
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (13 pp., HAL author manuscript of Tourneux 2003, Folia Orientalia 39: 123-135) opened with extracted text. p. 7 carries verbatim: "1.3. Touchant les tons / De nombreux changements tonals peuvent être observés dans nos exemples; le seul changement systématique que nous ayons pu observer est le remplacement du ton modulé descendant par un ton haut." followed by ex. 87 "médicament" (footnote 6 "Emprunt au kanuri") with old/young forms extracted as "kŒÀrgûÑ / kuÀrguÁÑ" (legacy phonetic font); the compiler kə̀rgûŋ / kùrgúŋ is a decoding of that, hence "minor differences" only in the transliteration of the example, not in the prose. p. 2 carries verbatim: "La langue, appelée [màlgbè], du mêm…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Malgbe is described as a tone language: every syllable in Tourneux's data carries a high or low tone, and older speakers also have a falling contour tone which younger speakers replace by high. No source opened says anything about word stress or accent in Malgbe, so no stress rule can be stated; the reading is 'tonal, no stress statement'.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tourneux notes numerous unsystematic tonal differences between old and young speakers; the falling tone > high change is the only systematic one.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated lexical items (nouns, verbs, adjectives) in citation form, transcribed in a simplified phonetic notation with tones; old-speaker vs young-speaker forms compared. No phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Tourneux 2003 describes the speech of Goulfey town (Cameroon), which the speakers call [màlgbè] — the nuclear variety, Glottolog dialect nucl1688 under malg1250. Bouny 1977 (not obtained) describes the 'mandagué de Mara', a different Malgbe dialect (Mara; Chad side), which Glottolog lists under malg1250 but which the earlier scan also attached to Afade (afad1236). Tourneux's 2021 review discusses tone and a possible 'accent' in Mpade/Makary Kotoko (mpad1242), a sister language, not Malgbe.

sources.note: First-hand description of Goulfey Malgbe [màlgbè] by Tourneux (fieldwork 1994, 2002); sections on consonants (phoneme table), vowels, tones (§1.3) and syllables. All data are tone-marked (H/L, plus a falling contour in old speakers' forms); §1.3 states the only systematic tonal change is falling tone > high. Stress/accent is never mentioned.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT 375. §8.4.3 Malgbe, pp. 216-217.
sources.note: 'Malgbe, also known as Goulfey, has not been the subject of any phonological study, except again for the comparative studies by Tourneux (2001; 2003). There is also a wordlist (Allison n.d.).' Gives consonant/vowel surface inventories only; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2021. Review of Sean Allison, A Grammar of Makary Kotoko (Brill 2020). Linguistique et Langues Africaines 7: 115-123. (halshs-03473316)
sources.note: About Mpade (Makary Kotoko, mpad1242), not Malgbe: two tone registers per Tourneux/Adam vs. three per Allison; Tourneux sketches a possible 'accent' (accented syllables) explaining mid-tone realisations, 'aujourd'hui une très faible valeur distinctive'. No Malgbe statement.
